A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniMamba and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and supplementary Sections A-C. All 13 pages of each version support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original UniMamba experiments on nuScenes, Waymo and Argoverse 2, together with component ablations, efficiency measurements and supplementary qualitative results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original UniMamba benchmark results, ablations, efficiency measurements and supplementary qualitative results.

M1.justification: The specified UniMamba modules, serialization, channel grouping and Equations (4)-(7) remain unchanged. However, Section 3.4 changes the detector being modified from DSVT to LION, while Appendix A still specifies DSVT's BEV backbone and detection head. The PDFs do not resolve whether this revises implementation attribution or changes the actual detector procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LiDAR-based 3D object detection on nuScenes, Waymo and Argoverse 2. The represented categories, domains and test scenarios are retained, including the supplementary nuScenes analyses.

E2.justification: Tables 1-3 substantially revise the comparator set, adding LION-Mamba on nuScenes and Argoverse 2, LION-Mamba-L and VoxelMamba on Waymo, and SAFDNet on nuScenes test. Removed comparisons include PointPillars, SASA, PVT-SSD and PillarNeXt on nuScenes validation; AFDetV2 on nuScenes test; and SWFormer, VoxelNeXt and PTv3 on Waymo. Direct Mamba competitors now participate in the principal comparisons.

E3.justification: Sections 3.4 and 4.2 revise the stated experimental setup from a DSVT/OpenPCDet basis to LION and replace the explicit 48/24/12-epoch schedule and nuScenes no-CBGS statement with hyperparameters following LION. This changes the reported configuration, without establishing specific replacement budgets or reruns. Splits, metrics, voxel sizes and stated test-time restrictions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The SLM/serialization, channel-group, feature-aggregation and efficiency analyses in Tables 4-7 are retained. Appendix B preserves the window/group-size, downsampling-stride and serialization-order ablations; Appendix C preserves the same SAFDNet qualitative comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: UniMamba's scores, shared baseline values, ablations and appendix findings remain unchanged. Added entries include LION-Mamba's 68.0 mAP on nuScenes validation and 41.5 mAP on Argoverse 2, LION-Mamba-L's 75.90 L2 mAP and VoxelMamba's 75.33 on Waymo, and SAFDNet's 68.3 mAP on nuScenes test. These additions and the removed comparator rows refine the comparative results without changing UniMamba's reported outcomes.

T1.justification: The SSM formulation and discretization, voxel/window definitions, and mathematical descriptions in Equations (1)-(7) retain their substance. Neither version adds formal assumptions, propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about combining convolution with bidirectional SSM, complementary serialization and local-global channel grouping. The three-benchmark effectiveness claim and 70.2 mAP nuScenes result are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations connecting locality, balanced local/global processing and hierarchical features to detection performance remain substantively unchanged, including Appendix B's sensitivity interpretations. No new applicability boundaries or limitations are introduced, and the discussion does not substantially interpret the newly added Mamba competitors.

D1.justification: v3 removes the direct Code & Models link, the OpenPCDet access citation, explicit training epochs and no-CBGS disclosure. It also deletes the explanation that serialization ablations used parameter-matched GSE-only models with two bidirectional SSM layers. Implementation attribution changes to LION; hardware, optimizer, voxel configurations and Appendix A's architectural details remain.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 newly positions UniMamba alongside LION's grouped RNN framework and VoxelMamba's group-free modeling. Section 3.3.1 explicitly credits LION and PTv3 for sparse-convolution positional information, and the implementation is attributed to LION. Additional vision references are introduced, while SASA, PillarNeXt, OpenPCDet and CBGS references disappear. These changes substantially revise the account of direct predecessors and intellectual lineage.

P1.justification: Localized rewriting affects the abstract, Mamba-related work, SLM explanation and implementation paragraphs, with several explanatory sentences shortened or removed. The section order, overall narrative and supplementary organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1-3 gain and lose comparator rows, with corresponding resizing and changes to best-score emphasis. Table 4 moves from page 8 to page 7, and the author block and surrounding text reflow. The architecture diagrams and supplementary qualitative figure remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Adding direct Mamba competitors and acknowledging relevant predecessors improves comparison coverage and attribution. However, v3 removes code-access and training/ablation details, while its LION implementation statements remain unexplained alongside Appendix A's retained DSVT specification. With UniMamba's results unchanged, these contextual gains, reproducibility losses and unresolved implementation ambiguity prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
